wu: Play 'Simon Says' with health commands: 'Simon says touch your head', 'Simon says pretend to cough', 'Simon says drink water'. Students stand and follow, sitting if they miss a command.
wuAlt: Play 'Charades' with illness actions: student mimes 'headache', 'stomachache', 'fever', others guess in English.
Do a quick 'Body Parts Quiz': teacher points to body parts, students shout the English word.
pres: Show flashcards of people with health problems (e.g., headache, cold). Elicit problems in Arabic/English, then model advice: 'You should rest', 'You shouldn't eat ice cream'. Check understanding with thumbs up/down for correct advice.
presAlt: Read a short dialogue between two friends: one says 'I have a sore throat', the other replies 'You should drink tea'. Highlight 'should/shouldn't'.
Use a role-play: teacher pretends to be sick, student gives advice using target language.
prac: Play 'Advice Relay': teams take turns drawing a health problem flashcard and saying 'You should...' or 'You shouldn't...'. Award points for correct sentences. Monitor and correct pronunciation.
pracAlt: Do 'Match the Problem to the Advice': worksheet with problems on one side, advice on the other; students draw lines.
Play 'Find Someone Who...': walk around asking 'Should I...?' about health habits, e.g., 'Should I eat vegetables?'
ls: Listen to a dialogue between a doctor and a patient. Students fill in gaps in a worksheet: 'You should ________' (rest), 'You shouldn't ________' (play sports). Check answers as a class.
re: Play 'Health Charades Relay': two lines of students race to mime a health problem (e.g., 'fever') and their partner guesses the word in English. First team to guess correctly wins a point.
prod: Pair role-play: Student A is a friend with a health problem (e.g., 'I can't sleep'), Student B gives 2-3 pieces of advice using 'should/shouldn't'. Swap roles. Encourage follow-up questions like 'Why?'
rw: Read a short 'Healthy Habits' leaflet. Underline all advice with 'should/shouldn't'. Then write 3 sentences about your own habits, e.g., 'I should drink more water'. Share with a partner.
st: Sing 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' with actions, then end with the goodbye routine: 'Today we learned to give health advice. Thank you, class!'
g: Teams race to say correct 'should/shouldn't' sentences for health problems.
Students mime illnesses for others to guess in English.
Match health problems to advice flashcards.
Ask classmates about health habits using 'should' questions.
Practice giving advice in pairs using problem cards.
diff: Fast finishers: write a 5-sentence paragraph about 'My best health advice'.
Support learners: use sentence starters like 'You should ________' on the board.
hw: Write 5 quiz questions about health advice, e.g., 'What should you do if you have a headache?'
Draw 3 pictures of health problems and write advice for each.
Interview a family member about their health habits and write 2 pieces of advice for them.
tip: Use Moroccan cultural references, e.g., 'You should drink mint tea for a sore throat', to make advice relatable. Avoid sensitive topics like alcohol or pork.
